\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}

\text{England and Spain only}&=29-12-2-8=7\\

&=\frac{18}{58}=\frac{9}{29}

The car manufacturer is developing a new model. The production goals are that the probability of model $Y$ requiring an oil change at any given six-month service will be $\frac{m}{m+n}$, the probability of model $Y$ requiring an air filter change will be $\frac{n}{m+n}$ and the probability of model $Y$ requiring both will be $\frac{1}{m+n}$, where $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}^{+}$.

answer.worked:
Let $A$ denote requiring an air filter change and $O$ denote requiring an oil change.

$$\begin{align*}P(A\cap O')&=P(A)-P(A\cap O)\\&=\frac{n}{m+n}-\frac{1}{m+n}\\&=\frac{n-1}{m+n}.\end{align*}$$

(A) 0.1
(B) 0.2
(C) 0.5
(D) 0.6

answer.worked:
Using the addition rule:
$$\begin{align*}P(A\cup B)&=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)\\0.5&=a+2a-0.1\\0.6&=3a\\a&=0.2\end{align*}$$
The answer is (B).

entries.description:
Multiplication Rule for Multistage Experiments
If two successive events A and B in a multistage experiment are independent, then:
P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B)
We can write P(A and B) as P(AB) and P(A, B) and P(A ∩ B).
Note that P(A and B) is not always equal to P(B and A) for multistage probability.
